root_cause.text: `gso_features_check()` in `net/core/dev.c` only examined the outer IPv6 network-header length when deciding whether `NETIF_F_IPV6_CSUM`-only devices must fall back from TSO/GSO, so tunneled IPv6 packets incorrectly bypassed the extension-header check and could be offloaded as if they had a plain IPv6 transport header.
root_cause.evidence: The patch replaces the old direct test on `skb_network_header_len(skb) != sizeof(struct ipv6hdr)` with `skb_gso_has_extension_hdr(skb)`, which explicitly checks `skb_inner_network_header_len(skb)` for encapsulated packets and treats packets with no inner network header as needing software GSO; the commit message says “For tunneled packets, the inner header length must be checked instead” and mentions RFC 6951 SCTP-in-UDP as a special case.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add detection of IPv6 extension headers in GSO skbs, including encapsulated packets, so feature handling can account for them correctly.
intent_record.what: A new static helper function, `skb_gso_has_extension_hdr(const struct sk_buff *skb)`, was added. It checks whether a GSO skb is IPv6/TCPv6 or IPv6/UDP-L4 and whether the relevant network header length is not equal to `sizeof(struct ipv6hdr)`, with separate handling for encapsulated and non-encapsulated skbs and header-set checks in each case.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this provides a way to detect skbs that carry IPv6 extension headers in the GSO path. The logic distinguishes normal and encapsulated packets, and only reports true when the packet appears to be IPv6-based GSO traffic with a network header length inconsistent with a plain IPv6 header, which can be used to alter feature handling for such packets.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use the IPv6 extension-header helper to correctly gate checksum and GSO offloads instead of manually duplicating the header checks.
intent_record.what: The IPv6 checksum/TSO eligibility check in gso_features_check() was simplified: the explicit conditions testing for TCPv6 or IPv6 UDP_L4 GSO, a set transport header, and an IPv6 network header length not equal to sizeof(struct ipv6hdr) were removed and replaced with a single call to skb_gso_has_extension_hdr(skb) under the same NETIF_F_IPV6_CSUM feature test.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now disables NETIF_F_IPV6_CSUM, NETIF_F_TSO6, and NETIF_F_GSO_UDP_L4 whenever the skb is determined to have IPv6 extension headers through the helper, instead of relying on a manually duplicated set of protocol and header-length checks. This changes feature masking behavior to use the centralized extension-header detection logic, preventing offload paths that are incompatible with IPv6 extension headers.

grouping_result.intent: Use the IPv6 extension-header helper to correctly gate checksum and GSO offloads instead of manually duplicating the header checks.

consistency_review.core_intent: Improve IPv6 packet feature handling by detecting extension headers so checksum and GSO offload gating is correct.

Since the grouping’s representative intent is narrower than the shared theme, the set is not perfectly coherent under that intent.

consistency_review.core_intent: Use IPv6 extension-header handling to correctly gate checksum and GSO offloads, including cases involving encapsulated packets.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly address the root cause by adding IPv6 extension-header detection for GSO/offload decisions, including encapsulated/tunneled packets, and by using that logic to correctly gate checksum and GSO offloads instead of relying only on the outer IPv6 header length.

candidates.rationale: This conditional is the gating logic for disabling IPv6 checksum/TSO/GSO offloads. In the pre-fix code it only checked the outer IPv6 network-header path via the subsequent length comparison, which failed to account for tunneled IPv6 packets with extension headers.

This part of the condition identifies TCPv6 GSO packets that are subject to the incorrect offload decision. It participates in the vulnerable logic that failed to reject tunneled IPv6 packets with extension headers.

This part of the condition covers UDP L4 GSO over IPv6, which was also gated by the same insufficient header-length check and could therefore be mis-offloaded when IPv6 extension headers were present.
This protocol check restricts the logic to IPv6 packets, but it does not distinguish plain IPv6 from tunneled/extension-header cases. It is part of the vulnerable decision path.

This pre-fix guard checked only that a transport header was set, which was not sufficient to detect IPv6 extension headers in encapsulated packets. The root cause is the missing extension-header handling in this check sequence.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the start of the vulnerable gating condition in gso_features_check(). It only participates in a manual header-length based check and, as described, failed to account for IPv6 extension headers in tunneled packets.
This branch identifies TCPv6 GSO traffic subject to the incorrect IPv6 offload decision. It is part of the condition that bypassed proper extension-header handling.
This branch includes UDP L4 GSO packets in the same flawed decision path. It was governed by the insufficient IPv6 header check and could incorrectly allow offload.
This IPv6 protocol test is part of the vulnerable logic, but by itself it did not detect tunneled IPv6 or extension headers, allowing the incorrect offload decision to proceed.
This guard only verified that a transport header was present; it did not verify absence of IPv6 extension headers, which is the root cause of the bug.
